ARG.blurb: Argentina is a serial currency-crisis case. It suffered the 2001-02 collapse of its dollar peg (the 'convertibility' crisis), a 2018 peso run, and a severe 2023 crisis with inflation over 100% that helped bring Javier Milei to power.

BRA.blurb: Brazil endured chronic hyperinflation through the 1980s and early 1990s, tamed only by the 1994 Real Plan. The real was then devalued sharply in January 1999 when its managed peg broke.

ECU.blurb: Ecuador abandoned its own currency entirely, adopting the US dollar in 2000 after a severe banking and currency crisis.

EGY.blurb: Egypt has repeatedly devalued the pound under IMF programmes, floating it in 2016 and again devaluing sharply in 2022-23 amid a foreign-currency shortage.

IDN.blurb: Indonesia was the hardest-hit victim of the 1997-98 Asian crisis: the rupiah lost most of its value, the economy contracted violently, and the turmoil helped end the Suharto era.

KOR.blurb: South Korea was a flashpoint of the 1997 Asian financial crisis: the won collapsed and the country needed a large IMF bailout. It recovered strongly and is now a high-income economy.

LKA.blurb: Sri Lanka suffered a severe economic and currency crisis in 2022, defaulting on external debt as the rupee collapsed amid a foreign-reserves shortage.

MWI.blurb: Malawi's kwacha has repeatedly come under pressure; the currency was devalued by around 44% in November 2023 amid a foreign-exchange shortage.

MYS.blurb: Malaysia was swept up in the 1997-98 Asian crisis; it controversially imposed capital controls and pegged the ringgit rather than take an IMF programme.

NGA.blurb: Nigeria, an oil exporter, has faced recurring naira devaluations when oil revenues fall - notably in 2016 and again in 2023 when the currency was sharply devalued.

PAK.blurb: Pakistan has faced recurrent balance-of-payments and currency pressure, with the rupee sliding through repeated IMF programmes.

RUS.blurb: Russia's rouble crashed in August 1998 when the government defaulted on domestic debt. The rouble fell again sharply in 2014-15 amid collapsing oil prices and sanctions.

SLV.blurb: El Salvador adopted the US dollar as its official currency in 2001, abandoning its own colon.

THA.blurb: Thailand was the epicentre of the 1997 Asian financial crisis: the baht's forced float in July 1997 triggered the region-wide contagion.

TUR.blurb: Turkey has repeated currency stress: a banking-driven crash in 2001, and a prolonged lira slide from 2018 onward as inflation surged and central-bank independence was questioned.

UKR.blurb: Ukraine's hryvnia has crashed during periods of political and military crisis - sharply in 2014-15 after the Maidan revolution and Russia's annexation of Crimea, and again after the 2022 invasion.

VEN.blurb: Venezuela experienced one of history's worst hyperinflations from around 2016, with the bolivar becoming almost worthless amid economic collapse; official data reporting itself broke down.

ZAF.blurb: South Africa's rand is one of the world's most volatile currencies, prone to sharp sell-offs during global risk-off episodes (notably 1998, 2001, 2008 and 2015).

ZWE.blurb: Zimbabwe experienced one of the most extreme hyperinflations ever recorded in the mid-to-late 2000s, culminating in the abandonment of its currency in 2009.
